status: Two independent full-text treatments were inspected for the A page, including complete lecture notes. Source fetch stamps and scoped validations are recorded after authoring; the arguments are locally conditional and no empirical result is asserted.

sources.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries
sources.locator: §1, PDF pp. 1–3; §3, PDF pp. 11–12; §4.1, PDF pp. 14–16; and Appendix F, PDF pp. 70–71.

contents.name: Group-like symmetry defects, codimension, topologicality, and fusion

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant introduction passage on PDF pp. 1–3 was read.
source_review.supports: A q-form symmetry is represented by codimension-(q+1) defects whose correlation functions are invariant under allowed deformation and whose fusion follows the group law.
source_review.limitations: The paper's general definition does not construct a continuum QFT or establish any specific defect realization.

contents.name: Exchange of q>0 defects and Abelianity of one group

source_review.read_extent: The complete kinematic argument in §3, PDF pp. 11–12, was read.
source_review.supports: The order of two codimension-greater-than-one group defects can be exchanged by an admissible deformation in the stated local setup.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem states the exchange isotopy explicitly and does not promote the argument to arbitrary global support networks.

contents.name: Magnetic U(1) surface operator and the flux of an external 't Hooft line

source_review.read_extent: The complete magnetic-current and surface-operator passage in §4.1, PDF pp. 14–16, was read.
source_review.supports: The current F/(2π) is closed by the Bianchi identity in the source-free pure U(1) model; a magnetic surface operator measures flux and 't Hooft lines carry magnetic charge.
source_review.limitations: The local example fixes its own 2π flux convention, external-line boundary data and conditional regulator scope.

contents.name: Representation-valued action of ordinary zero-form symmetries

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant ordinary-symmetry discussion in §2, PDF pp. 5–8, was read.
source_review.supports: Ordinary group elements act on local operators through group representations; the group itself may be non-Abelian.
source_review.limitations: The finite S3 representation and its irreducibility are established by the local matrix argument.

contents.name: Torsion-dependent electric and magnetic flux-operator commutator

source_review.read_extent: Appendix F, PDF pp. 70–71, including the Bockstein pairing and a torsion-cycle example, was read.
source_review.supports: Joint electric and magnetic flux operators can obey a torsion-pairing commutator on spatial manifolds with torsion cycles.
source_review.limitations: This is a mixed relation between distinct symmetry actions; it does not negate the conditional within-group exchange conclusion.

sources.title: Lakshya Bhardwaj, Lea E. Bottini, Ludovic Fraser-Taliente, Liam Gladden, Dewi S. W. Gould, Arthur Platschorre, and Hannah Tillim, Lectures on Generalized Symmetries
sources.locator: Full 150-page PDF retrieved; §§2.2.1–2.2.2, PDF pp. 12–20, and §4.1, PDF pp. 60–62.

contents.name: Definition of an invertible topological p-form defect and group fusion

source_review.read_extent: The complete §2.2.1 definition and properties, PDF pp. 12–14, were read.
source_review.supports: Invertibility, codimension-(p+1) support, topological deformation, group fusion, and the local exchange argument for p>=1.
source_review.limitations: The model-specific interface, background and boundary data are supplied explicitly in the local definition.

contents.name: Simple p-dimensional operators, scalar crossing action, and character charges

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant part of §2.2.2, PDF pp. 16–20, including the simple-operator crossing argument and character-group discussion, was read.
source_review.supports: A simple p-dimensional operator has scalar crossing action; fusion makes the scalar a one-dimensional character and its charge an element of the Pontryagin dual.
source_review.limitations: The local proof states unitarity, boundedness, continuity, and support-exchange hypotheses explicitly.

contents.name: Finite Z_N self-duality example for the Pontryagin dual
contents.reason: The theorem proves the general character-charge interface, while the worked B-page model uses compact U(1); a finite discrete gauge-theory realization is not constructed in this pair.

contents.name: Continuous and discrete higher-form background fields

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant continuous/discrete background definitions and gauge transformations in §4.1, PDF pp. 60–62, were read.
source_review.supports: Continuous backgrounds use degree-(p+1) connection data; finite discrete backgrounds use cochains, cocycle conditions when uncoupled, and coboundary gauge transformations.
source_review.limitations: The local definition leaves global transition, boundary, higher-group and coupling data to the selected model and claims no universal gauging.

contents.name: Finite Z_N characters and the U(1) magnetic-line charge

source_review.read_extent: The complete character examples in §2.2.2, PDF pp. 18–20, and Maxwell charge example through §2.2.2 Example 2.3, PDF pp. 20–21, were read.
source_review.supports: The U(1) character has integer charge and the magnetic charge of an external 't Hooft line is its magnetic higher-form charge.
source_review.limitations: The local item derives the phase with its own stated flux, orientation and smooth-chain Stokes conventions.

contents.name: Ordinary zero-form group representations on local operators

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant §2.1 treatment, PDF pp. 5–11, was read.
source_review.supports: Codimension-one symmetry defects fuse by the group law and local operators transform in representations of a possibly non-Abelian group.
source_review.limitations: The specific S3 representation decomposition is computed locally.

contents.name: Higher categorical charges for operators of dimension greater than p
contents.reason: This pair treats ordinary character charges of simple operators with dimension exactly p; higher categorical charge data require a separate supplier and are not used here.

contents.name: Higher-group modifications of the discrete background cocycle equation
contents.reason: Coupled 0-form and higher-form background data require their own local-coefficient and Postnikov proof; this pair records the interface but proves no higher-group consistency.

sources.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries

contents.name: Pure U(1) magnetic one-form current, surface defect and charged line

source_review.read_extent: The full magnetic-current and external-line argument in §4.1, PDF pp. 14–16, was read.
source_review.supports: The Bianchi-closed magnetic current, normalized surface operator, and magnetic charge of an external line.
source_review.limitations: The local calculation makes its compact U(1), 2pi flux, boundary and regulator inputs explicit.

contents.name: Ordinary group elements and representation-valued local-operator action

source_review.read_extent: The complete ordinary-symmetry treatment in §2, PDF pp. 5–8, was read.
source_review.supports: A zero-form group element acts through a representation on local operators.
source_review.limitations: The three-state S3 model and its irreducibility check are supplied by the local finite calculation.

contents.name: U(1) character charges and the Maxwell magnetic-line example

source_review.read_extent: The complete character examples and Maxwell higher-form charge example in §§2.2.2, PDF pp. 18–21, and the background example in §4.1, PDF pp. 60–61, were read.
source_review.supports: The Pontryagin dual charge convention and the magnetic charge of an external line.
source_review.limitations: The local proof independently evaluates the flux change using the pinned smooth-chain Stokes supplier.

contents.name: Finite Z_N self-duality example for the Pontryagin dual
contents.reason: The B page demonstrates the continuous U(1) flux character and a separate S3 zero-form representation; it does not construct a finite discrete gauge-theory realization.

contents.name: Zero-form topological operators and local representation actions

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant zero-form discussion in §2.1, PDF pp. 5–11, was read.
source_review.supports: Zero-form symmetry groups can be non-Abelian, and local operators transform in group representations.
source_review.limitations: The S3 matrices, noncommuting transpositions and two-dimensional irreducibility proof are local.
